title: Predicting What Comes Next: Exploring Sequences and Progressions

topics.title: Introduction to sequences and their notation

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the terms of a sequence using position notation such as t1, t2, ..., tn and distinguish finite from infinite sequences.
Describe the patterns in triangular and square numbers as sums of natural numbers and odd numbers.
Use an explicit formula in n to compute any term of a sequence directly.
Decide whether a number is a term of a sequence by solving tn = k for a natural number n.
Generate terms of a sequence from a recursive rule that relates each term to earlier terms.
Recognise the Virahanka-Fibonacci sequence, its rule Vn = Vn-1 + Vn-2 and its history.
Identify an arithmetic progression and its common difference, including negative differences.
Apply tn = a + (n - 1)d to find terms, positions and unknown first terms or differences of an AP.
Explain why the points (n, tn) of an AP lie on a straight line.

topics.title: Sum of the first n natural numbers

concepts.learning_objective: Derive and use Sn = n(n + 1)/2 by pairing the sum with its reverse.
Find the sum of a block of consecutive natural numbers as a difference of two such sums.
Identify a geometric progression by checking that the ratio of consecutive terms is constant.
Apply tn = ar^(n-1) to find terms and positions of terms in a GP.
Model repeated multiplication, such as the heights of a bouncing ball, with a GP.

topics.title: Fun with fractals: the Sierpinski triangle and carpet

concepts.learning_objective: Find the number of shaded pieces at each stage of a Sierpinski fractal as a GP.
Find the shaded area at each stage of a Sierpinski fractal and describe how it shrinks towards 0.
